haiku-low.q1: A PR runs an unpushed image build and make test-unit, with no registry push, cluster credentials or deploy. A push to main, which is a merge, starts a deployable run.
haiku-low.q2: Staging and production both deploy registry.internal/shop-api:SHA, built once per run. Nothing is rebuilt after the tests.
haiku-low.q3: Integration failure: one automatic whole-job retry; if that also fails, the run fails and the sibling is cancelled. Unit failure: no retry, run fails, sibling cancelled.
haiku-low.q4: Staging keeps running the new SHA with the schema left in place. Rollback sets the image to /deploy/staging/previous_tag in SSM, which holds the image it ran before.
haiku-low.q5: Only release-approvers may approve, and not the merged commit's author. If no approval comes within 72 h, the run expires, nothing reaches production, and #deploys is told.
haiku-low.q6: In SSM Parameter Store: /deploy/<env>/current_tag and previous_tag. deploy.sh writes them only after a rollout succeeds. The canary is never recorded.
haiku-low.q7: Stable keeps its old image, tags stay unwritten, and the new migration stays applied. The canary is removed, the run fails and is announced. A new commit is the fix.
haiku-low.q8: It ends quietly as superseded, with no announcement. Under the production lock it finds SHA is not a descendant of current_tag, then releases the lock.
haiku-low.q9: Outside the window it waits and re-checks every 5 min. If the lock is busy it queues. After taking the lock it re-checks the window, and if past 15:00 it releases and waits.
haiku-low.q10: The 1-minute 5xx ratio of shop-api-canary from Prometheus, checked every 30 s for 15 min after the first 60 s. A sample above 1%, or no or unreachable data, fails it.
haiku-low.q11: NOT STATED. The document does not say how approvers are notified or what information they see, beyond it being a CI manual job.
haiku-low.q12: Not automatically. Tags are not written, so previous_tag would be two versions old. The pipeline stops, announces, and a human decides; production also removes the canary.

sonnet.q1: A PR runs a build of the image (not pushed) and make test-unit (~4 min); no registry push, cluster credentials or deploy. A merge (any push) to main starts a run that can deploy.
sonnet.q2: Both deploy the same image registry.internal/shop-api:SHA (tag = merge commit SHA), built once in step 1. Nothing is rebuilt later in the run.
sonnet.q3: Integration test failure: the whole job is automatically retried once; if the retry fails, the run ends, the sibling is cancelled and #deploys is told. Unit test failure: no retry; the run fails immediately, the sibling job is cancelled and #deploys is told.
sonnet.q4: Staging is rolled back via deploy.sh rollback staging, which reads previous_tag from SSM and moves the image back to it (schema stays); current_tag is set to previous_tag. The run then ends, the lock is released and #deploys is told of the failure.
sonnet.q5: Only members of the release-approvers group, and not the author of the merged commit (an approval by the author is discarded and the run keeps waiting). If nobody approves within 72 h, the run expires, nothing goes to production (staging stays on SHA) and #deploys is told.
sonnet.q6: In SSM Parameter Store: /deploy/<env>/current_tag and /deploy/<env>/previous_tag. deploy.sh writes them (previous_tag = old current_tag, current_tag = SHA) only after the rollout succeeds. The canary is never recorded.
sonnet.q7: Stable deployment is unchanged. Tags are not written (the canary writes nothing to SSM). The canary is removed by canary-off. The production database keeps the new migrated schema (forward-only, not undone). #deploys is told the run failed; the fix is a new commit through the pipeline.
sonnet.q8: At the production supersede check (under the production-deploy lock) the run finds its SHA is not a descendant of current_tag and ends quietly as superseded, with no announcement and no deploy. Its approval request just goes stale and approving it is harmless.
sonnet.q9: Outside the window (Mon-Thu 09:00-15:00 UTC) it waits and re-checks every 5 min. Then it takes the production-deploy lock, queuing if another production deploy is running; after getting the lock it re-checks the window, and if outside it releases the lock and goes back to waiting. Then it does the supersede check and proceeds.
sonnet.q10: The canary's 5xx ratio (1-min rate of 5xx over all requests for app shop-api-canary), read from Prometheus by the pipeline's watch step every 30 s for 15 min from rollout ready, ignoring the first 60 s. Any single sample above 1% (0.01) fails; empty/no-data or unreachable Prometheus after warm-up also counts as a breach.
sonnet.q11: NOT STATED. The document says only that the approval is a manual CI job restricted to release-approvers, with CI recording who approved and when; it describes no notification to approvers and no information shown to them.
sonnet.q12: It is not returned automatically: no automatic rollback after a failed rollout. The pipeline stops, tags are not written, the canary is removed (production), #deploys is told, and a human decides. Reason: deploy.sh writes tags only after a successful rollout, so previous_tag would be two versions old and a wrong rollback target.
